index.title: 1. What is Blueprnt?
index.summary: Professional, high-performance, local-first desktop media workstage for photographers, DITs, and video editors — 100% offline, zero cloud, zero telemetry.
index.content:
Blueprnt is a professional, high-performance, local-first desktop media application engineered for photographers, Digital Imaging Technicians (DITs), video editors, and media catalog managers.

Blueprnt provides a zero-cloud, 100% offline desktop toolkit for high-throughput digital asset ingestion, cryptographic BLAKE3 checksum verification, multi-drive 3-2-1 backups, token-based batch renaming, cinema proxy transcoding, and EXIF/IPTC privacy scrubbing.

Core Pillars of Blueprnt:

• 100% Offline Local Data Sovereignty: Zero cloud tracking pixels, telemetry, or remote server dependencies. Every operation runs purely on your local CPU/GPU hardware.

• BLAKE3 Cryptographic Verification: Bit-by-bit binary checksum verification during card transfers to guarantee 100% data integrity before clearing memory cards.

• Instant Embedded Preview Extraction: Bypasses full-frame RAW sensor array decoding by seeking directly to container binary offsets (TIFF IFD tags and ISOBMFF container boxes) to extract embedded 1080p JPEG preview streams in sub-15ms windows.

• Indivisible Shot-Group Locking: Automatically detects and clusters multi-format capture files sharing a stem — treating RAW, JPG, HEIC, MOV, WAV voice memos, and sidecar XMP files as an atomic logical group. Renaming or modifying one asset automatically syncs all paired companion files without breaking Lightroom, Capture One, or Final Cut catalog paths.

• High-Throughput Parallel Processing: Multi-threaded directory walking and data stream parallelism to effortlessly handle shoots spanning 10,000+ files without UI freezes.

• Two-Stage Atomic File Replacement: Writes scrubbed, transcoded, and renamed binaries to .tmp_blueprnt intermediate paths before executing atomic filesystem swaps, protecting files against mid-flight power failures or system crashes.

• Persistent Undo Journal: Logs every batch rename, quarantine, and scrub into a local database running in Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) mode, guaranteeing 1-click reversibility across application restarts.

index.title: 2. Multi-Platform Installation Guide
index.summary: Native standalone installers for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows 10/11, and Linux (Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/RHEL). No runtime dependencies required.
index.content:
Blueprnt v1.5.0 is distributed as native standalone binaries for macOS, Windows, and Linux. No runtime dependencies (such as Node.js or Python) are required on the host system.

Download the official installer matching your operating system:

Operating System — Architecture — Installer Package
• macOS (12.0+) — Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) — Blueprnt_1.5.0_aarch64.dmg
• Windows (10/11) — x86_64 (64-bit) — Blueprnt_1.5.0_x64-setup.exe
• Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) — amd64 (64-bit) — Blueprnt_1.5.0_amd64.deb
• Linux (Fedora/RHEL) — x86_64 (64-bit) — Blueprnt-1.5.0-1.x86_64.rpm

---

2.1 macOS Installation (Apple Silicon)

Step 1: Download Blueprnt_1.5.0_aarch64.dmg from the official release page.
Step 2: Double-click the downloaded .dmg file in Finder to mount the disk image.
Step 3: Drag the Blueprnt application icon into the macOS Applications shortcut folder.
Step 4: Launch Blueprnt from Applications or Spotlight. On initial launch, macOS Gatekeeper may prompt verification — click 'Open' to proceed.
Step 5: Security & Storage Permissions: To allow Blueprnt to index external SD cards and SSDs, open macOS System Settings → Privacy & Security → Files and Folders, and ensure Blueprnt has permission for 'Removable Volumes' and 'Network Volumes' (or grant 'Full Disk Access').
Step 6: When hovering over the Blueprnt icon in the macOS Dock, the application name will display in proper title casing as 'Blueprnt'.

---

2.2 Windows Installation (Windows 10 / Windows 11)

Step 1: Download Blueprnt_1.5.0_x64-setup.exe from the official release page.
Step 2: Double-click the executable to launch the NSIS Setup Wizard. If Microsoft Defender SmartScreen presents a prompt, click 'More info' and then select 'Run anyway'.
Step 3: Select the destination directory (default is %LocalAppData%\Programs\Blueprnt) and choose whether to create a Desktop shortcut.
Step 4: Click 'Install' and allow the wizard to complete file extraction.
Step 5: Click 'Finish' to launch Blueprnt. Windows Taskbar and system tray tooltips will display as 'Blueprnt'.

---

2.3 Linux Installation (Debian / Ubuntu / Fedora / RHEL)

For Debian, Ubuntu, and Linux Mint:
  sudo dpkg -i Blueprnt_1.5.0_amd64.deb
  sudo apt-get install -f -y

For Fedora, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, and openSUSE:
  sudo dnf install ./Blueprnt-1.5.0-1.x86_64.rpm

[NOTE] Linux System Dependencies: Blueprnt requires libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 and libayatana-appindicator3-1 on Linux desktop environments. The package manager commands above automatically resolve these prerequisites.

index.title: 3.1 Media Indexer & Real-Time Analytics Dashboard
index.summary: Primary gateway for digital asset discovery: multi-threaded scanning, Radial SVG Sunburst visualizer, 6-metric analytics dashboard, and 1080p preview extraction.
index.content:
The Media Indexer serves as the primary gateway for all digital asset discovery. Utilizing multi-threaded directory walking, it indexes large cinema media cards and drive mounts in milliseconds, populating a rich telemetry suite.

Step 1: Mount your SD card, CFexpress card, RED Mini-Mag, or external NVMe drive to your workstation.
Step 2: Navigate to the 'Media Indexer' tab on the top navigation bar.
Step 3: Click the large 'Select Media Source Folder' button. A native system folder picker will appear.
Step 4: Select the root directory or DCIM folder of your source media and confirm.
Step 5: Instant Scanning — The engine scans all files in parallel, creating logical shot pairings and extracting embedded 1080p preview streams.

Step 6: Inspect the Real-Time Media Analytics Dashboard Cards:
• Total Assets: Total count of discovered media files.
• Stills & Photos: Total JPEG, PNG, TIFF, and standard photo files.
• RAW Negatives: Total camera RAW files (CR2/CR3/NEF/ARW/RAF/DNG).
• Live & Motion Photos: Paired Apple Live Photos and Android Motion Photos.
• Cinema Videos: Apple ProRes MOV, MP4, H.264/H.265 video files.
• Storage Payload Volume: Total storage footprint formatted cleanly in MB, GB, or TB.

Step 7: Radial SVG Sunburst Storage Visualizer: Click and hover over sectors in the interactive radial sunburst chart to explore proportional disk consumption categorized by media types and file extensions.

Step 8: Filter and Search: Use the search bar to locate specific filenames, camera models, or lens types instantly.

index.title: 3.2 Persistent System Settings & Studio Defaults
index.summary: Configure global studio policies: 3-2-1 backup routing, BLAKE3 cryptographic verification, default IPTC metadata templates, and persistent SQLite-stored studio defaults.
index.content:
The Settings Window configures global studio policies, automated 3-2-1 backup ingest routing, cryptographic verification rules, and default IPTC metadata templates that persist across all projects in the local database.

Step 1: Open Settings — Click the Gear icon located in the upper right header of the application window.

Step 2: Configure Storage Ingest Destinations (3-2-1 Backup Strategy):
• Primary Destination (Editing Work Drive): Set your high-speed internal NVMe SSD path where active editing assets will reside.
• Secondary Destination (3-2-1 Mirror Backup): Set an on-site secondary RAID array or external backup drive for simultaneous dual-write mirroring.
• Cloud Staging Directory: Set a local sync folder (e.g. Dropbox, Google Drive, Synology Drive) for automated off-site cloud replication.

Step 3: Toggle BLAKE3 Bit-by-Bit Verification: Enable the 'Cryptographic BLAKE3 Verification' toggle to enforce bit-level checksum checks after every file transfer, ensuring 100% data integrity with zero bit-rot.

Step 4: Configure Studio IPTC Metadata Defaults:
• Creator / Photographer Name (e.g. 'Jane Doe')
• Copyright Notice (e.g. '© 2026 VibePress Studio. All Rights Reserved.')
• Credit Line (e.g. 'VibePress Commercial Photography')
• Default Keywords (e.g. 'Commercial, 4K, Studio, Editorial')
• Studio Website URL (e.g. 'https://vibepressstudio.vercel.app')

Step 5: Click 'Save Settings'. All configurations are atomically written to the local database and immediately apply to all future ingestion operations.

index.title: 3.3 Token Pattern Builder & CSV Client Roster Engine
index.summary: Advanced EXIF-powered token naming engine with real-time collision-free preview projections and CSV client roster mapping for portrait, event, and real estate shoots.
index.content:
Blueprnt features an advanced token pattern engine that constructs dynamic, collision-free naming conventions from EXIF metadata, timestamps, camera models, sequence counters, custom text, and client rosters.

Available Token Tags:

{CustomText} — Custom user-defined text string
  Example output: VibePress_Master / ClientName

{Date:YYYY-MM-DD} — Capture date as Year-Month-Day
  Example output: 2026-09-20

{Date:YYYYMMDD} — Compact capture date without hyphens
  Example output: 20260920

{Time:HHmmss} — Capture time as Hours-Minutes-Seconds
  Example output: 143502

{Model} — Camera body hardware model from EXIF
  Example output: Canon_EOS_R5 / Sony_A7R5

{Lens} — Lens optical specification from EXIF
  Example output: 24-70mm_F2.8

{ISO} — Sensor sensitivity rating from EXIF
  Example output: ISO400

{Sequence:03} — Zero-padded 3-digit numerical sequence
  Example output: 001, 002, 003...

{Sequence:04} — Zero-padded 4-digit numerical sequence
  Example output: 0001, 0002, 0003...

{Original} — Original source filename stem prior to renaming
  Example output: IMG_9482

{RosterName} — Client name mapped from uploaded CSV roster range
  Example output: Sarah_Jenkins / Unit_104

---

Step-by-Step CustomText Token Configuration:
1. In Settings or the Organize & Rename tab, locate the 'CustomText Value' input box.
2. Type your desired custom identifier (e.g. 'SmithWedding_Day1' or 'Architectural_Master').
3. Click the '{CustomText}' quick token chip to append it to your active naming pattern.
4. The token engine immediately updates the live renaming projection table in real time.

---

Step-by-Step CSV Client Roster Mapping Workflow:
1. For school portraits, sports events, or real estate shoots, prepare a standard CSV file with headers: SequenceStart, SequenceEnd, ClientName (e.g. 1, 25, 'Smith_Family'; 26, 60, 'Johnson_Family').
2. In the Token Builder, click 'Upload Client Roster (CSV)'.
3. Select your .csv file. The engine validates sequence boundaries and maps {RosterName} tokens dynamically to matching shot indices.
4. Inspect the preview table to verify that every client name aligns perfectly with their capture sequence.

index.title: 3.4 Organize & Rename Tab
index.summary: Live non-destructive renaming projection grid with pre-flight collision detection, atomic two-stage execution, shot-pair preservation, and 1-click SQLite journal rollback.
index.content:
The Organize & Rename workspace provides a live, non-destructive renaming projection grid with built-in pre-flight collision detection, atomic two-stage execution, and instant undo journal rollback.

Step 1: Navigate to the 'Organize & Rename' tab.

Step 2: Inspect the Live 'Renaming Projection' Grid:
• Original Name & Path: Shows current physical filename and subfolder location.
• Target Naming Projection: Displays the real-time evaluated filename based on your active token pattern.
• Status Column: Displays an emerald 'READY' badge for conflict-free assets, or a vibrant rose 'COLLISION' badge if a name conflict is detected.

Step 3: Proactive Pre-Flight Collision Prevention: If two files project to the same target name or if a target file already exists on physical storage, Blueprnt highlights the collision and disables the execution button, preventing accidental data overwrites.

Step 4: Select Assets to Rename: Check individual checkboxes to rename specific assets, or check the header checkbox to select all filtered items.

Step 5: Execute Atomic Rename: Click 'Execute Bulk Rename'. Blueprnt performs a safe Two-Stage Temporary Move (.tmp_blueprnt intermediate paths) to guarantee that circular naming swaps execute cleanly without collisions.

Step 6: Atomic Shot-Pair Preservation: Paired RAW + JPG + HEIC + MOV + XMP sidecars share the identical logical_group_id and are renamed synchronously, preserving Lightroom and Capture One catalog paths.

Step 7: Delete Unneeded Files to OS Trash: Select unwanted files and click 'Delete Selected → Trash'. Files are safely moved to the operating system's Trash, and records are synchronously purged.

Step 8: Persistent Undo Journal (1-Click Rollback): Click the History icon to open the Undo History Modal. View past executed batches with timestamps and click 'Undo Batch' to revert filenames instantly.

index.title: 3.5–3.6 Video Transcoder & Editing Proxies
index.summary: Batch video transcoding studio for Apple ProRes 422/HQ/Proxy, Avid DNxHR, H.264, and H.265 proxies with real-time fps telemetry and NLE-ready stem-matched output.
index.content:
Configure default video transcoding profiles and hardware acceleration options in the Settings Window to ensure seamless proxy generation for Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and Final Cut Pro.

Supported Proxy Codec Profiles:

• Apple ProRes 422 (Proxy) — ~45 Mbps at 1080p — Final Cut Pro / Premiere / Resolve
  Ultra-fast timeline scrubbing, minimal CPU/GPU overhead.

• Apple ProRes 422 (LT) — ~100 Mbps at 1080p — Commercial Dailies & Review
  Balanced visual fidelity for client review cuts.

• Apple ProRes 422 (HQ) — ~220 Mbps at 1080p — Master Delivery & VFX
  Highest quality 10-bit color proxy mastering.

• Avid DNxHR (LB) — Low Bandwidth Profile — Avid Media Composer / DaVinci Resolve
  Standard offline editing proxy for broadcast pipelines.

• Avid DNxHR (SQ) — Standard Quality Profile — Broadcast Delivery & Multi-Cam
  High-efficiency 8-bit standard editing codec.

• H.264 (AVC / MP4) — CRF 22 / Hardware NVENC/VT — Web Delivery & Mobile Review
  Universal compatibility across mobile and web players.

• H.265 (HEVC / MP4) — CRF 26 / 10-bit HDR — Archival & Storage Pools
  Maximum compression efficiency with minimal file size.

[PRO-TIP] Audio Downmixing & Resolution Scaling: In Settings, set Resolution Scale to '50% (Half-Res)' or '1080p' for optimal editing performance on laptop workstations. Ensure 'Stereo Downmix (2.0 Channel)' is checked if shooting with 4-channel cinema audio.

---

Transcoder & Proxies Tab — Step-by-Step:

Step 1: Navigate to the 'Transcoder & Proxies' tab.
Step 2: Review the automatically populated video queue containing all indexed cinema and drone video clips.
Step 3: Select your target proxy profile (e.g. 'ProRes 422 Proxy - 1080p' or 'H.264 Web Proxy').
Step 4: Set proxy output destination (default creates an organized /Proxies subfolder alongside primary media).
Step 5: Click 'Start Batch Transcoding'.
Step 6: Monitor Real-Time Processing Telemetry:
  • Individual Clip Progress Bar (0% to 100%)
  • Processing Speed (e.g. 145 fps / 6.0x realtime)
  • Elapsed Time and Estimated Time Remaining (ETA)
  • Current encoding resolution and audio downmix status

Step 7: Upon completion, proxy filenames match the original source stems exactly, enabling seamless 1-click proxy attachment inside DaVinci Resolve, Adobe Premiere Pro, and Apple Final Cut Pro.

index.title: 3.7 Deduplication Tab & Delete Confirmation
index.summary: Cryptographic BLAKE3 exact duplicate discovery combined with temporal burst clustering, Smart-Keep heuristics, non-destructive Quarantine Vault, and safe OS Trash deletion.
index.content:
The Deduplication workspace combines cryptographic BLAKE3 byte-by-byte duplicate discovery with temporal burst clustering to identify redundant takes, burst sequences, and duplicate files across multiple storage media.

Step 1: Navigate to the 'Deduplication' tab.

Step 2: Choose your analysis mode:
• Exact BLAKE3 Duplicate Finder: Compares cryptographic checksums to find 100% byte-for-byte identical files across cards and folders.
• Temporal Burst Clustering: Groups high-speed burst shots sharing the same camera model captured within a configurable time delta (0.5s to 5.0s).

Step 3: Smart-Keep Heuristics: Blueprnt automatically evaluates burst clusters and flags the highest-resolution frame or largest file size as the recommended 'Keeper' (green badge), while staging redundant shots for quarantine or deletion.

Step 4: Non-Destructive Quarantine Vault: Click 'Move to Quarantine Vault' to safely move redundant files into an isolated _Quarantine directory while strictly preserving the original nested subfolder tree.

Step 5: Safe Deletion with Confirmation Window: Click 'Delete Selected Duplicates'.
• The Delete Confirmation Dialog appears displaying the exact count of selected files and the total storage volume to be reclaimed.
• Confirming deletion moves the files to the operating system's native Trash (zero hard erasure risk) and purges records synchronously.

index.title: 3.8 Deep Metadata Editor Tab
index.summary: Full-featured workspace for in-place EXIF, IPTC, and XMP manipulation, GPS purge, DateTimeOriginal correction, and studio branding injection with atomic two-stage binary replacement.
index.content:
The Deep Metadata Editor is a dedicated full-featured workspace for direct, in-place EXIF, IPTC, and XMP metadata manipulation, original capture date/time modification, and complete privacy sanitization.

Step 1: Navigate to the 'Deep Metadata Editor' tab.

Step 2: Select a media file or multiple files from the left asset list.

Step 3: Modify Original Content Creation Date & Time:
• In the 'Content Creation Date' section, use the interactive date and time pickers to adjust DateTimeOriginal and CreateDate timestamps.
• Perfect for synchronizing camera bodies whose internal clocks drifted during multi-camera shoots.

Step 4: One-Click Complete GPS Purge:
• Click the vibrant red 'Purge All GPS & Location Data' button.
• The engine instantly removes Latitude, Longitude, Altitude, GPS Satellites, and location timestamps from EXIF and XMP sidecars.
• Green verification badges confirm that zero location trace remains.

Step 5: Edit Studio IPTC & XMP Metadata Fields In-Place:
• Artist / Photographer Name
• Copyright Notice & License Terms
• Credit Line & Digital Source Type
• Document Title & Description / Caption
• Camera Body & Optical Lens Model Strings

Step 6: Click 'Save & Update Metadata In-Place'. Changes are written cleanly to file headers using atomic two-stage binary replacement, updating the UI immediately.

index.title: 4. Operational Best Practices & FAQ
index.summary: Expert answers on Lightroom/Capture One catalog integrity, power-failure crash protection, optimal hardware ingestion speeds, and cloud privacy confirmation.
index.content:
Q: How does Blueprnt ensure that renaming a RAW file does not break my Lightroom or Capture One catalog?

A: Blueprnt enforces Indivisible Shot-Group Locking (logical_group_id). When you rename or move a RAW file (e.g. IMG_9482.CR3), the engine atomically mutates all associated companion files (IMG_9482.JPG, IMG_9482.XMP, IMG_9482.MOV, IMG_9482.WAV) using identical naming stems in the same transaction. This preserves sidecar associations and catalog integrity perfectly.

---

Q: What happens if my computer loses power during a 500-file batch rename or metadata update?

A: Blueprnt uses a Two-Stage Temporary File Replacement architecture. Files are initially written to intermediate paths (.tmp_blueprnt) and validated before executing atomic OS-level filesystem renames. Furthermore, every batch is recorded in the local Undo Journal (blueprnt_state.db), allowing you to reopen Blueprnt and immediately view or reverse the operation with 1 click.

---

Q: What hardware setup provides the fastest ingestion speeds?

A: For maximum throughput, ingest media directly from high-speed UHS-II / CFexpress Type B USB 3.2 Gen 2 or Thunderbolt card readers directly to an internal PCIe Gen 4/5 NVMe SSD. Blueprnt's multi-threaded pipeline will saturate hardware bus speeds effortlessly.

---

Q: Does Blueprnt transmit any of my images, EXIF data, or license details to the cloud?

A: No. Blueprnt is strictly 100% local-first. All preview extraction, BLAKE3 checksum calculations, proxy transcoding, and database operations execute purely on your local CPU/GPU hardware. License verification uses secure offline Ed25519 cryptographic tokens stored in your native OS Keyring.

---

Q: Can I use Blueprnt without a license key during evaluation?

A: Yes. Blueprnt includes a full 15-day free evaluation trial with completely unrestricted access to all features — including Rename Pro, Video Transcoding, and Deep Metadata Editing — starting automatically from your first launch. No credit card or account is required to evaluate the software.

---

Q: What file formats does Blueprnt support for RAW import?

A: Blueprnt natively supports Canon CR2 and CR3, Nikon NEF, Sony ARW, Apple HEIC/HEIF, standard JPEG, TIFF, PNG, and all major video formats including Apple ProRes MOV, H.264 MP4, H.265 HEVC, RED R3D, and ARRI footage entirely on the local file system without any network APIs.

index.title: 2. Why is This Plugin Important?
index.summary: 5 critical operational pillars: CTR lift (+25% to 40%), commission theft protection, Amazon ToS compliance, SEO safety, and zero link rot.
index.content:
In affiliate marketing and digital publishing, the difference between a failing site and a high-revenue publication often comes down to trust, deliverability, compliance, and link maintenance.

1. Significant Click-Through Rate (CTR) Lift (+25% to 40%):
Online visitors have grown hyper-skeptical of long, messy URLs loaded with tracking queries, affiliate hashes, and strange foreign domains. Branded links matching your website domain (e.g., yoursite.com/go/product) look official, safe, and curated. Industry studies consistently show that branded cloaked links achieve 25% to 40% higher click-through rates compared to raw affiliate URLs.

2. Commission Theft & Scraping Protection:
Malicious browser extensions, link scrapers, and unscrupulous aggregators actively hunt for raw affiliate IDs in webpage code to overwrite or strip them. Cloaking hides your affiliate IDs behind internal server redirects, ensuring your attribution cookies remain intact and your rightful commissions reach your payout account.

3. Protection Against Merchant Account Bans (Amazon Compliance):
Merchant programs like Amazon Associates Operating Agreement (Section 6) explicitly forbid disguising, cloaking, or hiding affiliate destinations. Publishers who cloak Amazon links risk immediate account termination and permanent forfeiture of unpaid earnings. VibePress Affiliate Link Cloaker solves this with Smart ToS Uncloaking: it recognizes Amazon, eBay, and Target links, rendering them as raw, direct links on the front end while maintaining asynchronous click analytics in your dashboard.

4. Search Engine Optimization & Crawl Budget Protection:
Unflagged commercial outbound links can trigger Google manual action penalties for unnatural outbound linking. This plugin automatically applies rel="nofollow", rel="sponsored", and X-Robots-Tag: noindex headers, instructing search engine spiders not to pass PageRank or waste crawl budget indexing empty redirect scripts.

5. Elimination of Catastrophic Link Rot:
When an affiliate merchant abruptly shuts down, pauses their affiliate program, or changes landing page URL structures, publishers face a nightmare: hundreds of dead links across thousands of legacy blog posts. Without a centralized cloaking engine, updating them requires days of manual editing. With this plugin, changing the destination URL once inside the dashboard instantly updates every mention site-wide.

index.title: 7. Technical Architecture & Database Schema
index.summary: Deep dive into the native WordPress CPT schema, rewrite engines, transient caching, and click analytics pipeline.
index.content:
Under the Hood Architecture:

1. Native WordPress Custom Post Type (salc_link):
VibePress Affiliate Link Cloaker avoids complex proprietary database tables for core link records. Each cloaked link is stored as a native WordPress post (post_type = 'salc_link') in wp_posts, with metadata stored in wp_postmeta. This ensures 100% compatibility with WordPress backup plugins, migration tools, WP-CLI, and native caching engines.

2. Priority Rewrite Engine (RewriteEngine.php):
Registers top-priority rewrite rules (^go/([^/]+)/?$) on init, routing cloaked URLs directly through template_redirect:1. Database lookups are accelerated with 24-hour WordPress Transients (salc_link_slug_{slug}), reducing server query overhead to near zero.

3. Redirect Engine & Header Lifecycle (RedirectEngine.php):
Hooks template_redirect with priority 1. Resolves destination URLs, executes A/B rotation rules, evaluates client-side conditional device/OS parameters, appends forwarded UTM queries, sets X-Robots-Tag: noindex headers, and issues HTTP 307 (or 301/302/200 iFrame) responses.

4. Bot-Filtered Analytics Pipeline (ClickTracker.php):
Logs click events to local table wp_salc_clicks with bot filtering (filtering out 30+ search engine spiders and scrapers), GDPR IPv4/IPv6 IP anonymization (stripping the last octet), and Cloudflare geo resolution.

5. Smart Compliance & Beacon Layer (SmartUncloaker.php & uncloak-beacon.js):
Parses post content on the_content:15. If a link matches Amazon, eBay, or Target regex, it dynamically swaps the href to the raw destination while appending data-salc-uncloaked="1". When clicked, navigator.sendBeacon sends click telemetry to POST /wp-json/salc/v1/track without redirecting, fully satisfying Amazon Associates Operating Agreement §6.

index.title: 8. Glossary of Key Terms
index.summary: 18 official definitions for link cloaking, redirects, compliance, tracking beacons, and automation concepts.
index.content:
Official Definitions of Key Concepts:

• Link Cloaking: The process of masking an external affiliate URL behind a branded URL hosted on your primary domain.
• Custom Slug: The unique keyword identifier at the end of a URL path (e.g. in yoursite.com/go/bluehost, bluehost is the slug).
• URL Prefix: The parent directory preceding cloaked links (e.g., /go/, /recommends/, /deal/).
• HTTP 301 Redirect (Permanent): Tells browsers and search engines that a page has moved permanently; heavily cached by web browsers.
• HTTP 302 / 307 Redirect (Temporary): Informs browsers to query the server on every single click; prevents stale destination cache issues (307 is the industry standard for affiliate marketing).
• iFrame Masking: Opening a merchant sales page inside a full-width HTML container while keeping your own domain visible in the browser address bar.
• rel="nofollow": An HTML attribute instructing search engines that your site does not endorse or pass PageRank to the destination URL.
• rel="sponsored": Google's official attribute designating that a link is commercial, compensated, or an affiliate hyperlink.
• X-Robots-Tag: noindex: An HTTP header instructing search engine spiders not to index redirect pages in Google search results.
• Smart Uncloaking: A dynamic script that uncloaks affiliate links for restricted merchants (like Amazon) into raw URLs on the front end to maintain ToS compliance.
• Tracking Beacon: A lightweight JavaScript mechanism (navigator.sendBeacon) that logs visitor click analytics asynchronously in the background.
• A/B Split Testing: Distributing incoming clicks across multiple target URLs by weighted percentage to measure conversion rate differences.
• Deal Expiration: Automatically disabling or rerouting affiliate links once a calendar date or click limit is exceeded.
• Fallback URL: A backup destination URL used when an affiliate deal expires or a merchant link fails.
• Broken Link Scanner: An automated cron script that pings target merchant URLs to verify they return an OK 200 response.
• DOM-Safe Keyword Auto-Linker: A tool that scans article copy and automatically hyperlinks target keywords to affiliate URLs without corrupting HTML tags or headings.
• UTM Forwarding: Dynamically passing tracking parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, etc.) from incoming visitor links through to merchant URLs.
• Custom Post Type (CPT): WordPress's native content structure (salc_link), ensuring high-speed queries and universal theme/plugin compatibility.

index.title: 9. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ Guide)
index.summary: 15 in-depth questions and answers across General & Setup, Redirects, SEO, Link Management, and Migration.
index.content:
General & Setup

Q1: How do I install and activate the plugin?
A: Download the plugin ZIP file, log in to your WordPress dashboard, navigate to Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin, upload the ZIP, and click Activate. Once active, you will see the new Link Cloaker item in your WordPress admin menu.

Q2: Will cloaking affiliate links slow down my website?
A: No. VibePress Affiliate Link Cloaker is built for high speed. Redirect lookups use native WordPress post IDs paired with WordPress Transients (cached database lookups), executing redirects in milliseconds with negligible server overhead.

Q3: Where did the plugin menu go? I can't find 'Affiliate Links'.
A: The menu is named 'Link Cloaker' in your WordPress admin sidebar. All submenus (All Links, Add New Link, Categories, Tags, Statistics, Tools & Migration, Settings, Documentation) are grouped directly beneath it.

Redirects & Performance

Q4: What is the difference between a 301, 302, and 307 redirect?
A: • 301 (Permanent): Browser caches this redirect aggressively. If you ever change the affiliate destination URL later, visitors' browsers may still take them to the old URL.
• 302 (Found / Temporary): Bypasses browser cache, checking the server on each click.
• 307 (Temporary Redirect): The gold standard for affiliate links. It bypasses browser cache, forces a live server lookup on every click, and guarantees complete preservation of HTTP request headers.

Q5: What is iFrame Masking and when should I use it?
A: iFrame Masking displays the merchant's landing page inside an embedded container on your site, keeping yoursite.com/go/deal in the visitor's address bar. It is ideal for linking to documentation, web calculators, or client onboarding tools where you want to maintain your brand visibility. Note: Some merchants (such as Amazon and financial institutions) prohibit iFraming via X-Frame-Options headers.

SEO & Compliance

Q6: Will cloaking affiliate links hurt my Google search rankings?
A: No—in fact, it protects them. The plugin automatically adds rel="nofollow sponsored" attributes and X-Robots-Tag: noindex headers, fully complying with Google Search Essentials. This prevents search engines from penalizing your site for thin affiliate content or unnatural outbound links.

Q7: Is cloaking permitted by Amazon Associates?
A: Amazon Associates Operating Agreement Section 6 prohibits disguising or cloaking affiliate links. However, VibePress Affiliate Link Cloaker features Smart ToS Uncloaking. When enabled in Link Cloaker -> Settings, any link pointing to Amazon is dynamically uncloaked on your public website into an approved, direct Amazon affiliate link, while preserving background click tracking.

Q8: How does the FTC Auto-Disclosure work?
A: The plugin detects whether a blog post or page contains cloaked affiliate links. If detected, it automatically injects a styled compliance notice (e.g. 'This post contains affiliate links...') at the top or bottom of your post, fulfilling Federal Trade Commission disclosure regulations.

Link Management & Automation

Q9: What happens when an affiliate offer expires?
A: You can set an Expiration Date or Max Clicks Threshold on any link. Once reached, the plugin will automatically redirect visitors to your specified Fallback URL (such as your homepage or a general deals category) or display a custom 'Deal Expired' notice.

Q10: How does the DOM-Safe Keyword Auto-Linker work?
A: Under Link Cloaker -> Settings, you can specify keywords (e.g., 'Bluehost') and link them to an affiliate URL. The plugin automatically parses your articles and converts matching text into affiliate links, while strictly respecting your configured limits (e.g., maximum 3 links per post) and never corrupting HTML headings, images, or existing anchors.

Q11: How does A/B traffic rotation work?
A: On the link edit screen under A/B Split Testing & Traffic Rotation, you can enter multiple merchant URLs and assign percentage weights (e.g. 70% to Vendor A, 30% to Vendor B). Incoming traffic is split dynamically, allowing you to test which vendor yields higher conversions.

Migration & Integrations

Q12: Can I migrate my existing links from Pretty Links or ThirstyAffiliates?
A: Yes. Navigate to Link Cloaker -> Tools & Migration and click Platform Migration Engine. The plugin automatically scans your database for Pretty Links or ThirstyAffiliates data and imports all titles, slugs, destinations, and historical click counts with a single click.

Q13: Can I import and export links using CSV spreadsheets?
A: Yes. Under Link Cloaker -> Tools & Migration -> CSV Import & Export, you can upload a CSV spreadsheet to batch-create hundreds of links instantly. You can also export click logs into CSV format directly from the Statistics page.

Q14: How does the Stripe Payment Link feature work?
A: By entering your Stripe API Secret Key in Link Cloaker -> Settings, you can turn any cloaked link into a direct checkout session. When a visitor clicks the link, they are taken directly to Stripe's hosted 1-click checkout. Once the transaction completes, your dashboard logs conversion count and dollar revenue via Stripe webhooks.

Q15: How does the plugin comply with GDPR privacy laws?
A: Under Link Cloaker -> Settings -> Privacy & GDPR Compliance, you can enable Anonymize Visitor IP Addresses. This automatically strips the last octet from visitor IPv4 (e.g. 192.168.1.0) and IPv6 addresses prior to database logging, ensuring full compliance with European GDPR and California CCPA guidelines.
